name: Cherokee County, GA
findings: Cherokee County has 704 nonprofit organizations. 275 of them (39%) list at least one way to get involved in their tax returns or on their websites: membership, volunteering, public events, or civic and political action.
The most common is membership, listed by 198 organizations.
Religious organizations are the largest group offering opportunities (28% of those with an identified type).
Compared with 10 similar places, Cherokee County has about as many organizations offering opportunities per resident.

observations.title: Few arts and cultural organizations list public events
observations.text: 1 arts and cultural organization here list public events. In similar places of this size, about 8 would.

confidence.text: Based on 8 organizations here; 39% of all organizations here have no identified type.

observations.question: Do people here look for public events through arts and cultural groups? Where else does that happen?

observations.title: Fewer organizations list civic or political action
observations.text: Per resident, fewer organizations in Cherokee County list civic or political action in their tax returns or on their websites than in 10 similar places (about 63% of the typical level).

confidence.text: Based on 10 organizations here; 39% of all organizations here have no identified type.

observations.question: Does that match what people here experience? Where do people find ways to take civic or political action now, including outside formal organizations?

observations.title: Religious organizations that list no opportunities
observations.text: 71 religious organizations here list none of the four kinds of opportunity in their tax returns or on their websites. Many may still offer them without describing them there.

confidence.text: Based on 71 organizations here; 39% of all organizations here have no identified type.

observations.question: What do religious organizations here do in the community? How do people find out about them?
